changes: Rescue: when the whole-photo grid cannot be verified, rerun Moku v4 on closer and rotated views around the densest stone detections, then on views re-framed around the best grid so far
Line check: the board's own grid lines confirm the stone grid, replace it when they clearly disagree, or the photo is refused
Echo filter (board.ECHO = 0.9): a weaker detection within 0.9 squares of a stronger stone is kept only if its own intersection shows that colour
A dense board that reads as nearly empty is refused instead of returned
Orientation and corner fallback from the previous pipeline are kept

references.userSource: Photos 1-5: screenshots from a separate paid recognition tool supplied by the user. Photo 6: 12 points corrected by assistant visual inspection, not independently verified. Photo 6 was scored from a re-saved copy because the original file could not be read on this machine.
references.webSource: Public web photos transcribed by hand; kept outside the repository

method.upload: Same as the page: longest edge up to 3072 pixels, JPEG quality 0.88, reduced by 0.8 until at most 1,050,000 bytes
method.machine: Local Apple Silicon CPU, ONNX Runtime

localTimeSeconds.note: Single-thread worst case 5.5-6.6 s; normal photos run Moku 6 times, rescued photos 9 times, at most 13

angledPhotos.method: Opt-in TILT conditions in real_photos.py: synthetic perspective warps of the same photos (tilt20, tilt35, tilt50 from the bottom edge; side30 from one side)
angledPhotos.caveat: Warping an already angled real photo (photo 6 is taken at a low angle with people at the table) exaggerates the angle further; synthetic warps do not reproduce real stone heights and occlusion
angledPhotos.decision: Not pursued. Strongly angled photos remain unreliable; the page asks for a photo taken from above

hardPhotos.finding: Remaining errors on photo 5 come from glare and colour casts on stones (bright125 10, cool 7)
hardPhotos.decision: Not pursued. Further threshold tuning on 6 photos risks overfitting; users must compare the board with the photo

live.result: Photos 1-4 and 6 exact; photo 5 two extra white stones (same as local)
live.decision: Use 3,538 MB with 2 threads and a 20-second timeout: about 1.65 times faster for about 17% more cost per photo, and the 13-run worst case (about 12 s) stays well inside the timeout

caveats: Six user photos and ten web photos cannot establish general accuracy; recognition remains experimental
Thresholds were developed on these photos, so there is a risk of overfitting
The photo 6 reference was corrected visually by the assistant and is not independently verified
